verdict.headline: GitHub OAuth apps are completely self-serve with zero manual review needed, but GitHub strongly prefers GitHub Apps for fine-grained scopes.
verdict.timeToFirstConnection: 10–15 minutes to register an app and obtain client credentials.
verdict.timeToProduction: Same day for personal accounts; organization access requires an org owner to approve the app.
verdict.handsOnEffort: Under 30 minutes to configure callback URLs and scope strings.
verdict.biggestRisk: OAuth apps grant broad, broad access across whole accounts (e.g., full read/write on all repos) and org access blocks users unless an admin approves.

ownAppDecision.summary: You can start immediately with Composio's managed GitHub app, but registering your own is self-serve and necessary if you need your own custom app identity.
reasons: Composio offers managed OAuth credentials so you can start testing GitHub integrations immediately without setting up Developer Settings.
Registering your own GitHub OAuth app is completely free and requires no waiting or external verification.
You will need your own app if you require custom branding on the consent prompt or dedicated rate limit buckets.

phases.name: Preparation & Decision
phases.goal: Decide between a classic OAuth App and a GitHub App, and gather callback parameters.

steps.title: Choose OAuth App vs. GitHub App
steps.detail: Evaluate if classic OAuth scopes (e.g. broad 'repo' scope) suit your agent, or if fine-grained repository permissions (GitHub App) are required.
steps.agentHelp: Summarize architecture trade-offs between GitHub Apps and OAuth Apps for the target agent workflows.

steps.title: Define Redirect URIs and Scopes
steps.detail: Prepare up to 10 valid authorization callback URLs (loopback IP addresses are supported). Determine required scopes such as 'repo' or 'user:email'.
steps.agentHelp: Draft the exact minimal list of scope strings and validate the formatting of redirect URIs.

phases.name: App Registration & Integration
phases.goal: Register the app in GitHub Developer settings and execute the OAuth flow.

steps.title: Register New OAuth Application
steps.detail: Go to GitHub -> Settings -> Developer settings -> OAuth apps -> New OAuth App. Enter Application Name, Homepage URL, Application Description, and Callback URL.
steps.agentHelp: Pre-fill form values or generate step-by-step instructions for navigating GitHub Developer settings.

steps.title: Generate Client Secret and Store Credentials
steps.detail: Generate a new Client Secret from the app management page and securely store Client ID and Client Secret in environment variables.
steps.agentHelp: Generate sample configuration files or secret manager integration code.

steps.title: Implement Authorization Code Exchange
steps.detail: Direct users to the authorization URL, handle the callback code, and POST to https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token to get gho_ tokens.
steps.agentHelp: Generate complete OAuth 2.0 flow code including exchange handling and optional 8-hour expiring token refreshes.

phases.name: Production Launch & Org Approvals
phases.goal: Allow external users and organization members to connect seamlessly.

steps.title: Handle Organization Access Restrictions
steps.detail: Ensure end users know that if their org restricts OAuth apps, they must click 'Request access' during the OAuth flow for org owners to approve.
steps.agentHelp: Draft user-facing instructions and admin-consent request templates for organization owners.

steps.title: Monitor Token Limits and API Quotas
steps.detail: Track API requests against the standard 5,000 req/hr user bucket and ensure fewer than 10 active tokens are generated per user/app/scope combination.
steps.agentHelp: Build rate-limit monitoring and token reuse logic to avoid generating duplicate tokens.

requirements.detail: You must have a verified email on GitHub to create or authorize OAuth apps.
When an organization has access restrictions enabled, an org owner must approve the OAuth app before it can access org resources.

permissions.name: repo
permissions.purpose: Full access to public and private repositories, including code read/write, commit statuses, webhooks, and settings.
permissions.notes: Cannot be scoped to read-only for OAuth apps; grants wide write privileges.

permissions.name: workflow
permissions.notes: Required if the agent modifies .github/workflows content.

permissions.name: read:user / user:email
permissions.purpose: Read user profile data and primary/protected email addresses.
permissions.notes: Used for identifying the authenticated user.

permissions.name: admin:repo_hook / write:repo_hook
permissions.notes: Allows event triggers without full repo control if repo scope isn't granted.

nuances.title: Broad Permission Model
nuances.detail: OAuth apps grant wide broad permissions across all accessible repos; GitHub recommends GitHub Apps if targeted repository permissions are needed.

nuances.title: Per-User Token Caps
nuances.detail: GitHub limits to 10 active tokens per user/app/scope combination. Issuing an 11th automatically revokes the oldest token.

nuances.title: Rate Limits Share User Quota
nuances.detail: OAuth token calls count directly against the individual user's standard REST API rate limit (5,000 requests/hr).

blockers.symptom: End user authorizes the app, but organization resources/repositories are invisible or return 404 errors.
blockers.howToProceed: The user must request access for their organization during the consent flow, or an org owner must approve the application in Organization Settings -> OAuth application policy.

blockers.symptom: User sees error during authorization: 'This account is flagged, and therefore cannot authorize a third party application'.
blockers.howToProceed: The user must submit an appeal to GitHub Support/Reinstatement; the app developer cannot fix this.

agentCan: Draft required scope lists and parse space-separated scope strings
Generate OAuth 2.0 authorization request URLs and token exchange logic
Implement token refresh handling if expiring tokens are enabled
Detect rate-limit response headers and implement retry backoff
youMust: Log into GitHub and register the application in Developer settings
Generate and copy the Client Secret safely to secure environment storage
Obtain approval from GitHub organization owners if accessing private org resources

I am setting up [APP_NAME] to help with [USE_CASE_DESCRIPTION]. When connecting my GitHub account, organization access restrictions prevented [APP_NAME] from interacting with our organization's repositories.

Could you please approve [APP_NAME] under Organization Settings -> OAuth application policy? You can review the requested scopes ([REQUESTED_SCOPES]) and details here: [APP_WEBSITE_OR_URL].

Thanks,
[YOUR_NAME]

drafts.title: User Setup Instructions for Org Consent
drafts.purpose: In-app copy explaining why org repositories might not show up
drafts.content:
Connecting to GitHub Organization Repositories:

If your organization has OAuth restrictions enabled, you will see a 'Grant' or 'Request' button next to your organization's name during GitHub authorization. Please click 'Grant' (if you are an owner) or 'Request' so your administrator can approve access for [APP_NAME].

claimChecks.claim: Broad Permission Model: OAuth apps grant wide broad permissions across all accessible repos; GitHub recommends GitHub Apps if targeted repository permissions are needed.
claimChecks.evidence: In general, GitHub Apps are preferred to OAuth apps because they use fine-grained permissions, give more control over which repositories the app can access, and use short-lived tokens.

claimChecks.evidence: When OAuth app access restrictions are enabled, organization members and outside collaborators cannot authorize OAuth app access to organization resources.
